statusNote: Private Catholic university sponsored by the Archdiocese of Miami since 1988; standalone institution, not part of a multi-campus system.

leaders.priorTitle: Vicar General, Chancellor and Moderator of the Curia
leaders.notes: Monsignor Casale led STU for 24 years, its longest presidential tenure, before retiring in January 2018.
STU's tenth president; began official duties August 2018, formally installed in 2019. Previously grew enrollment and facilities at Thomas More College from 2013-2018.

statusNote: Standalone New Jersey state public university (not part of a governing university system); known as Richard Stockton College of New Jersey until 2015.

leaders.notes: Stockton's longest-serving president to date (20 years); retired to Galloway Township, NJ and died in 2009 after a brief illness.
Resigned in April 2015 amid controversy over Stockton's plan to buy the shuttered Showboat casino in Atlantic City.

leaders.nextRole: President Emeritus / Tenured Professor of Education
leaders.notes: Named acting president April 2015, interim president September 2015, and permanent president December 2015 amid the Showboat crisis; a member of Stockton's first entering class in 1971. Retired June 30, 2023 and stayed on as a professor.
Named Stockton's sixth president March 3, 2023; took office July 1, 2023 after leading Southern Connecticut State University from 2016-2023.
Longtime Suffolk figure (law professor from 1956, law dean from 1972) who led the university 21 years; retired in October 2010 at age 79 and was named President Emeritus.
Served as interim president bridging the Sargent-to-McCarthy transition; later became president of Mount Ida College in Newton, MA.

leaders.notes: Suffolk's ninth president; abruptly replaced by the board in August 2014, about a year before his contract ended, amid enrollment and financial pressures. Official reason given was to pursue other opportunities.
Veteran educator brought in as interim president to stabilize Suffolk after McCarthy's abrupt departure.

Suffolk's tenth president; led Lesley University for 22 years before Suffolk. Board voted to fire her in early 2016 after roughly one year, following disputed allegations of spending and management conduct; she left office July 2016.

Joined Suffolk as provost in 2014 (previously provost/VP at Ithaca College, 2011-2014); named acting president in 2016 after McKenna's departure, then appointed Suffolk's eleventh, and current, president in March 2018.

statusNote: Small private for-profit online distance-education system (Lakewood, CO/Santa Ana, CA) comprising William Howard Taft University and the separately-run Taft Law School (an unaccredited-by-ABA correspondence law school, split off in 2008 but under common ownership); accredited only by the Distance Education Accrediting Commission, not a traditional research institution. Public leadership records are very sparse online -- only the current and immediate-prior president could be reliably identified; earlier history (this is billed as only the '3rd President' of WHTU) could not be confirmed from public sources despite extensive searching.

leaders.notes: INFERRED/LOW CONFIDENCE: identified in various listings as WHTU's president (described as '3rd President') prior to Amy Kahn, holding a PhD from Colorado State University; exact start year for the presidency is not documented publicly (a 2020 company press release lists him only as media contact/Chief Academic Officer, not president, suggesting his presidency began close to 2021-2022). He appears to have continued at TUS afterward as Chief Academic Officer.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of Academic Affairs and Chief Academic Officer
leaders.notes: Became President and Chief Academic Officer of William Howard Taft University around April 2023; also referred to in company materials as the '3rd President' of WHTU.
